_doc: Bot cycle 40: manual review of every guard-passing swap (verdict accept/reject + why) and of high-overlap deck pairs. Read by scripts/grixis_refine.py; guidance, written from Oracle text and the cited EDHREC numbers.

Abaddon_the_Despoiler|Mystic Remora|Stor.why: Abaddon's cascade X is the life opponents lost this turn. Stormfist's upkeep trigger makes each opponent lose 1 before your first main phase, so from that turn on every hand spell up to MV 3 cascades without needing another damage source; it also draws for you every upkeep. Remora draws only off opponents' noncreature spells and never turns on Abaddon. Abaddon decks play Stormfist 48.0% vs Remora 12.6%; rank 2,011 is within the guard.

Goben__Gene_Splice_Savant|Mystic Remora|.why: Green Goblin gives every nonland card in the graveyard mayhem and makes graveyard casts cost {2} less. Thrill of Possibility's discard is a cost, so the discarded card becomes castable from the graveyard at a discount the same turn: it draws two and turns the commander on, at instant speed. Mystic Remora only draws off opponents' noncreature spells and never interacts with the commander. Norman Osborn decks play Thrill 37.6% vs Remora 19.2%; overall ranks 212 vs 101 (both staple tier).

Evelyn__the_Covetous|Reanimate|Cordial V.why: This Evelyn list is a cEDH reanimator/Thoracle build (Entomb, Unmarked Grave, Animate Dead, Necromancy, Worldgorger Dragon). Reanimate is a 1-mana piece of that core. Cordial Vampire is one more Vampire trigger for Evelyn but a 2-mana +1/+1-counter body that does not advance any win line: a power downgrade at this ceiling despite its synergy.

Dr__Eggman|Roaming Throne|Steel Overseer.why: Roaming Throne naming Human or Scientist makes Dr. Eggman's end-step trigger (draw, then each opponent faces a villainous choice) trigger twice. That is the commander's own engine, so it is not generic filler. Steel Overseer only pumps artifact creatures. The cut rule now protects trigger doublers.

Evelyn__the_Covetous|Reanimate|Blood Art.why: Same as Cordial Vampire: Reanimate is part of the reanimator core (now protected); Blood Artist is a drain payoff the list has no sacrifice engine for.

Marchesa__Dealer_of_Death|Mystic Remora|.why: Probe passes the guard (37.4% vs 14.4% of Marchesa decks) and is a free crime cantrip. But the source names Mystic Remora one of the list's card-advantage pillars, and records the list as matching a 2026-10-11 tournament-winning configuration. One extra crime trigger does not clearly outdraw Remora over the early turns at a cEDH table. Precision over speed: no swap without clear evidence.

Nathan_Drake__Treasure_Hunter|Reanimate|.why: Nathan's exile-and-cast trigger fires on attack whether or not he is blocked, and he already has first strike. Aqueous Form adds unblockability and scry 1 per attack: a small gain. Reanimate is a 1-mana answer that can take the best creature from any graveyard. Not clearly more in this deck.

Obeka__Brute_Chronologist|Reanimate|Fait.why: The list runs a reanimation package (Animate Dead, Necromancy, Frantic Search). Reanimate is its cheapest payoff; Faithless Looting is only an enabler that costs a card. Obeka's end-the-turn ability makes you discard to hand size, which does not need looting. Swapping a payoff for an enabler adds no power.

Obeka__Splitter_of_Seconds|Mana Drain|La.why: Lavaspur Boots' haste lets Obeka connect the turn she lands, which helps her combat-damage upkeep trigger. But Mana Drain is real stack interaction, and ward {1} only taxes a removal spell; the guard read Boots' ward as a counterspell, and that role match is now excluded. Losing a hard counter is a downgrade.

Sauron__Lord_of_the_Rings|Mystic Remora|.why: Consider (surveil 1, draw) barely feeds Sauron's own mill-five recursion. Mystic Remora draws several cards in the early turns at a Bracket 4 table. Not clearly more.

Sauron__Lord_of_the_Rings|Windfall|Deep.why: Windfall discards hands, which fills the graveyard with targets for the list's Entomb / Animate Dead / Necromancy / Reanimate package and Sauron's own return. Deep Analysis only draws (flashback after a mill is minor). Windfall is the reanimator-relevant card.

Sauron__Lord_of_the_Rings|Windfall|Consi.why: Same as Deep Analysis. Windfall's discard fills the graveyard for the reanimation package and Sauron's return; Consider surveils one card. Not clearly more.

Sauron__Lord_of_the_Rings|Windfall|Palan.why: Windfall is now protected as part of the discard-to-graveyard reanimation core. Palantír of Orthanc mills and draws slowly each end step, which does not do more than a one-shot hand refill that also stocks the graveyard.

Kess, Dissident Mage / Kefka, Court Mage.shared: 56 nonland cards: 8 fast-mana pieces, the cEDH free-interaction/tutor core (Fierce Guardianship, Pact of Negation, Mindbreak Trap, Deflecting Swat, Demonic/Vampiric/Mystical Tutor, Imperial Seal) and the Ad Nauseam / Tainted Pact / Thassa's Oracle / Brain Freeze win package; 22 shared cards match both commanders' Oracle hooks
Kess, Dissident Mage / Kefka, Court Mage.verdict: Partly homogenization. For Kess ("Once during each of your turns, you may cast an instant or sorcery spell from your graveyard") the instant/sorcery-heavy cEDH core is identity-driven: every shared spell is a second use from the graveyard. For Kefka the same spells are generic: his Oracle text ("each player discards a card" on enter/attack; "Whenever an opponent loses life during your turn, you draw that many cards") is served only by the Kefka-only cards (Waste Not, Tinybones, Bauble Burglar, Culling the Weak), not by the shared win package (Brain Freeze 22.0%, Borne Upon a Wind 17.9%, Final Fortune 11.1% on Kefka's EDHREC page).
Kess, Dissident Mage / Kefka, Court Mage.proposals: For Kefka's batch (guidance; each goes through the power guard and a written review): Final Fortune → Liliana's Caress (Kefka's discard makes each opponent lose 2, and on your turn Kefka then draws that many; 33.4% of Kefka decks), Borne Upon a Wind → Monument to Endurance (every discard from Kefka's trigger draws or makes Treasure; 37.8%), Brain Freeze → Dauthi Voidwalker (discarded cards are exiled with void counters for you to cast; 33.1%). Kess: no change; the overlap is her identity.

Cormela, Glamour Thief / Kess, Dissident.shared: 54 nonland cards; 40 of them match both commanders' instant/sorcery hooks, 13 are fast mana plus Rhystic Study and Thassa's Oracle
Cormela, Glamour Thief / Kess, Dissident.verdict: Identity-justified. Both commanders are instant/sorcery engines: Cormela's mana is "Spend this mana only to cast instant and/or sorcery spells" and she returns an instant or sorcery when she dies; Kess recasts them from the graveyard. Each keeps its own line: Cormela has storm and copy (Tendrils of Agony, Dualcaster Mage, Birgi, Seething Song) and altars, Kess has graveyard setup (Snapcaster Mage, Gifts Ungiven, Intuition, Dragon's Rage Channeler). The shared fast mana is ceiling-appropriate for two cEDH lists.
Cormela, Glamour Thief / Kess, Dissident.proposals: None. Re-check Cormela's Rhystic Study slot in her batch only if the guard finds a stronger instant/sorcery payoff.

Jeleva, Nephalia's Scourge / Kess, Dissi.shared: 55 nonland cards; 36 match both commanders' instant/sorcery hooks, 14 are fast mana plus Rhystic Study and Thassa's Oracle
Jeleva, Nephalia's Scourge / Kess, Dissi.verdict: Identity-justified. Jeleva casts "an instant or sorcery spell from among cards exiled with Jeleva without paying its mana cost", so the same dense spell suite is her engine too. Her unique cards are Jeleva-specific: library manipulation for her exile (Scroll Rack, Sensei's Divining Top, Lim-Dûl's Vault, Long-Term Plans) and big free spells (Mind's Desire, Doomsday, Peer into the Abyss).
Jeleva, Nephalia's Scourge / Kess, Dissi.proposals: None. The overlap is the shared spellslinger identity, not a generic shell.

Evelyn__the_Covetous.why: 1-mana piece of the list's Entomb / Unmarked Grave reanimator core; replacing it with a Vampire is a downgrade at this cEDH ceiling.

Sauron__Lord_of_the_Rings.why: Discards every hand into graveyards for the Entomb / Buried Alive / Animate Dead / Necromancy / Reanimate package and Sauron's cast-trigger return.

hook.label: discard (hand-picked)
hook.commander_text: Whenever Kefka enters or attacks, each player discards a card.
hook.card_text: Whenever an opponent discards a card, that player loses 2 life.

Kefka__Court_Mage.why: Every Kefka enter/attack trigger makes each opponent discard, so Caress drains 2 from each opponent per trigger. With the list's Wheel of Fortune, Windfall-style wheels and Gamble-style discards it threatens a lethal drain without combat. After Kefka transforms, his back face draws a card for each point of life an opponent loses during your turn. Final Fortune is a one-turn gamble that loses the game if the combo fails. 33.4% of Kefka decks play Caress against 11.1% for Final Fortune (overall ranks 2,404 vs 1,531, within the guard). It also removes an extra-turn card.

hook.label: discard (hand-picked)
hook.commander_text: Whenever Kefka enters or attacks, each player discards a card.
hook.card_text: Whenever you discard a card, choose one that hasn't been chosen this turn

Kefka__Court_Mage.why: Kefka's trigger also makes you discard, as do the list's Wheel of Fortune, Gamble, Jeska's Will and Lion's Eye Diamond / Underworld Breach loops. Each discard turn gives up to three modes: draw, Treasure, and each opponent loses 3 (that loss also feeds Kefka's back face). Mystic Remora only draws off opponents' noncreature spells and costs upkeep. Kefka decks play Monument 37.8% vs Remora 35.3%; ranks 930 vs 101 are within the guard. The proposal was Borne Upon a Wind, but that card stays: it is one of the list's two ways to cast spells as though they had flash for the instant-speed combo turns.

hook.label: discard (hand-picked)
hook.commander_text: Whenever Kefka enters or attacks, each player discards a card.
hook.card_text: If a card would be put into an opponent's graveyard from anywhere, instead exile it with a void counter on it.

Kefka__Court_Mage.why: Kefka forces opponents to discard every enter and attack, and Brain Freeze mills them. With Dauthi those cards are exiled with void counters instead, and Dauthi can be sacrificed to play the best one for free. It also turns off opposing graveyard engines. Valley Floodcaller is a second flash enabler that Borne Upon a Wind already covers. Kefka decks play Dauthi 33.1% vs Floodcaller 16.1%; overall rank 395 vs 761. The proposal was Brain Freeze, but that card is a piece of the list's Underworld Breach + Lion's Eye Diamond / Lotus Petal combos and stays.

hook.label: damage to an opponent → discard (hand-picked)
hook.commander_text: Whenever Nicol Bolas deals damage to an opponent, that player discards their hand.
hook.card_text: Whenever an opponent discards a card, this enchantment deals 2 damage to that player.

Nicol_Bolas.why: Each time Nicol Bolas deals damage to an opponent, that player discards their whole hand. With Megrim each discarded card deals 2, so one hit on a 5-card hand is 10 extra damage. The list already plays Liliana's Caress, Raiders' Wake and Waste Not, and Megrim is the redundant copy of that payoff. No Mercy only deters attackers, so it is defensive. 31.8% of Nicol Bolas decks play Megrim vs 7.3% for No Mercy; ranks 2,598 vs 1,455 are within the guard, and MV drops from 4 to 3.

Evelyn__the_Covetous.verdict: identity-first rebuild assessed, list left unchanged and flagged
Evelyn__the_Covetous.tradeoff: Evelyn's engine is "Once each turn, you may play a card from exile with a collection counter on it", so extra Vampire-enters triggers in one turn only add to the exile pool, not to plays. The list's best line is the cEDH core: Worldgorger Dragon + Animate Dead / Necromancy / Dance of the Dead, Thassa's Oracle + Tainted Pact / Demonic Consultation, and Underworld Breach + Brain Freeze. Evelyn adds one flash card-advantage play per turn from any library. Every Vampire or flicker card on her EDHREC page was checked against the list's weakest slots. Cordial Vampire, Blood Artist, Captivating Vampire, Bloodline Keeper and Dusk Legion Zealot (overall ranks 142–5,228) only fit by replacing a 1-mana combo or protection piece (Reanimate, Defense Grid, Culling the Weak, Vexing Bauble) and fail the power guard or role parity. Viscera Seer (rank 257) is the closest, but it would replace Defense Grid's protection for the combo turn. An identity-first Vampire version would clearly be weaker at the source's stated cEDH ceiling, so no swap is made. Flag: the commander contributes value, not the win line. Revisit if a cEDH-grade Vampire or exile-play payoff is printed.

Marchesa__Dealer_of_Death.verdict: identity confirmed after a scoring fix, list left unchanged
Marchesa__Dealer_of_Death.tradeoff: The 14% score was our gap, not the list's. Marchesa triggers on "Whenever you commit a crime", and the reminder text says targeting opponents, anything they control, or cards in their graveyards counts. Most of the list's cEDH interaction (targeted counterspells, bounce, removal) plus Spatial Binding, Hex Parasite, Spellskite, Tezzeret and Lapis Lazuli Talisman commit crimes. A new crimes hook now counts them. The source records this list as matching the 2026-10-11 Takeda Ryuhei tournament-winning configuration and keeps Lapis deliberately: it turns blue spells into targeted untaps, which are crimes. Considered and not made: Gitaxian Probe (a free crime cantrip, 37.4% of Marchesa decks) for Mystic Remora, Lapis Lazuli Talisman or Last Chance. It passes the guard, but each cut is a deliberate source decision (Remora: card-advantage pillar; Lapis: crime density; Last Chance: finisher), and Probe does not clearly do more. No swap.

Nicol_Bolas.verdict: identity confirmed after a scoring fix; 1 hand-picked swap
Nicol_Bolas.tradeoff: The 31% score was mostly our gap. Nicol's trigger is "Whenever Nicol Bolas deals damage to an opponent", and the combat hook did not cover it until this cycle. The list is already built to make him connect or deal damage: Lightning Greaves, Swiftfoot Boots, Sword of Feast and Famine, Pain for All, Chandra's Ignition, Kediss, Emberclaw Familiar. It also punishes the hand discard: Liliana's Caress, Raiders' Wake, Waste Not, the Tinybones pair, Torment of Hailfire. Pain for All, Chandra's Ignition and Kediss look generic, but each makes Nicol himself deal damage to an opponent, so they stay. One change: No Mercy (defensive) → Megrim (another discard payoff).
